intended_object: The local W^{1,p} extension operator through one Lipschitz boundary chart: for a chart (rigid coordinates e, L-Lipschitz graph φ, radii a, b) of an open Ω ⊆ ℝ × E and a smooth cutoff ψ supported in the shortened cylinder, the bounded linear map u ↦ (reflection extension of ψu across the graph, in chart coordinates, transported back), from W^{1,p}(Ω) to W^{1,p}(ℝ × E), equal to ψu on Ω. This is the boundary piece of the classical Sobolev extension operator (Evans §5.4; Evans–Gariepy §4.4). Inferred from the docstring and module documentation.
explanation: The body composes three operators in the right order. (1) `W1p.lipschitzChartLocalizeL` restricts u to Ω ∩ (chart region), multiplies by ψ, extends by zero inside the chart epigraph and pulls back by e.symm, giving a W^{1,p} function on the epigraph of φ in chart coordinates. (2) `W1p.normalEpigraphExtensionL` flattens the graph, extends by even reflection and unflattens; this is the standard bi-Lipschitz reflection for Lipschitz graphs. (3) `W1p.compAffineIsometryEquivL e` precomposes with e, so the value at x is the extended function at e x, i.e. it returns to the original coordinates. The shortened support condition (cylinder of radii a − 2Lb and b) is exactly what keeps reflected points inside the chart cylinder; the file proves this (`graphReflection_mem_normalCylinder`), and without it the extension would not restrict to ψu. The bound M on |ψ| and ‖∇ψ‖ over Ω only enters the boundedness proofs, not the operator's values. The companion lemmas confirm the intended behaviour: the result restricts to ψu on Ω, vanishes outside the chart cylinder, and has operator norm at most 4M(1+L)². The setting ℝ × E, with E a finite-dimensional real inner product space, Lebesgue measure and 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, is the natural one for Lipschitz-domain extension: finite dimension is needed for Lebesgue measure and the graph-flattening change of variables. Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces or extension operators, so there is no counterpart. Caveat: one could argue this is only an auxiliary step toward the global extension operator (which would make it not_a_mathematical_object), but it is the standard named local-extension construction from the textbook proofs and it is correctly implemented.
